title: The overview is not one screen in a maximised 1080p window (1920×950) for 6 of the 30 pairs where both champions have checked notes, including the priority pairs Ambessa vs Mordekaiser and Ambessa vs Ornn. The always-visible Sources control drops below the fold
detail:
Steps: Player Mode, open /resources/matchups?champion=Ambessa&vs=Mordekaiser in Chromium at 1920×950, 100% zoom, sidebar open. WebKit gives the same numbers.

Page scroll measured (scrollHeight − clientHeight):
- Ambessa vs Mordekaiser: 63px
- Ambessa vs Ornn: 43px
- Mordekaiser vs Ambessa: 54px
- Mordekaiser vs Ornn: 104px
- Ornn vs Mordekaiser: 104px
- Ornn vs Ambessa: 34px

What the owner sees: the Level changes panel lists every level note of both champions, unfolded (Mordekaiser's 3 plus Ornn's 2 or Ambessa's 2). It ends at 898–968px. The 'Sources and notices' control sits at 911–981 / 953–1023px. In the Ambessa vs Mordekaiser screenshot only its top border shows at the 950px edge, and in the Mordekaiser vs Ornn screenshot it is entirely below. The right column ends at 708–739px, so about 220px stays empty there.

Other sizes:
- 1440×900: the same six scroll 76–139px, and Riven vs Ornn scrolls 8px.
- 1920×1080: they fit, with only 57–127px left.
- 2560×1440 and 3440×1440: they fit.

Why nothing caught it:
- The docs measured 20 hand-picked pairs ('20 of 20' fit at 1920×950).
- e2e/matchup-intel-dashboard.spec.ts FIT_PAIRS (19 pairs) contains none of the six.
- The spec comment says 'Ornn vs Gwen is the tallest'. That is wrong: at 1920×950 Ornn vs Gwen leaves 102px and Mordekaiser vs Ornn is −73px.

Evidence (in (coordinator scratch)/mi-review2-owner/):
- checked30/results.json
- verify/Ambessa-vs-Mordekaiser__1920x950.png
- checked30/Mordekaiser-vs-Ornn__1920x950.png
- sweep/ambessa-1920x950.json (all 173 enemies)
fix:
- Fold level notes beyond two behind their count, as lane points and interactions already are, or let Level changes use the right column's spare height when the left column is taller.
- Add the six pairs, or all 30 checked pairs, to FIT_PAIRS.
- Correct the 'tallest' claim in the spec and in docs/MATCHUP_INTEL.md.
- Re-measure all five sizes.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. It reproduces exactly, it comes from this branch, it fails the branch's own stated target, and the main claim is read correctly.

Setup: the server on :3871 runs the 2dd104b7 build (BUILD_ID written 02:18, after that commit; 9cce9a33 only touches docs/MATCHUP_INTEL.md). Player Mode, /resources/matchups. On this build /matchup-intel returns 404. Chromium, 1920x950, sidebar open.

- **All 30 checked pairs:** exactly six scroll. Ambessa vs Mordekaiser 63, Ambessa vs Ornn 43, Mordekaiser vs Ambessa 54, Mordekaiser vs Ornn 104, Ornn vs Mordekaiser 104, Ornn vs Ambessa 34. The other 24 scroll 0.
- **WebKit:** 63/43/55/104/104/34.
- **Boxes:** Level changes ends at 897.9–968px. The right column ends at 707.5–738.6px. The Sources box spans 911.2–953 down to 981.2–1023.1px.
- **Fonts and pictures don't explain it:** Inter is the app's own local font and was loaded, so text measures the same on Windows and macOS. Blocking the pictures still gives 63px.
- **Other sizes:** at 1440x900 the six scroll 76–139px and Riven vs Ornn 8px. At 1920x1080, 2560x1440 and 3440x1440 they fit.
- **Sidebar collapsed:** 4 of the 6 still scroll (18–50px), and the Mordekaiser vs Ornn summary still ends at 957px.

Why it counts:
- 1920x950 is the branch's own named target ("a maximised window on a 1080p screen"). It is in the docs table, in the e2e SIZES list, and in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md ("fits one viewport from 1920 × 1080 (a maximised 1920 × 950 window included)").
- Owner decision 14 puts Sources "always on the screen, its one-line summary visible". The spec checks this as sources-summary bottom ≤ innerHeight.
- Ambessa is one of the owner's priority champions, and Mordekaiser and Ornn are the curated top-lane enemies.
- A real maximised window on a 1080p screen is about 917–976px tall, and all six still scroll in that range.
- Cause: the six are exactly the pairs between Ambessa (2 level notes), Mordekaiser (3) and Ornn (2). LevelNotesPanel lists all 4–5 notes unfolded, so the left column gets taller than the screen.
- None of the six pairs appear in FIT_PAIRS, the other specs or the docs.
- The import won't change it: these six champions use their checked facts, and level notes come only from checked notes.

Where the finding overstates:
- The Sources summary is unreadable in 4 of the 6. It is wholly below the fold in Ambessa vs Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser vs Ornn and Ornn vs Mordekaiser, and cut in half in Mordekaiser vs Ambessa.
- In Ambessa vs Ornn and Ornn vs Ambessa the summary line stays visible (bottom at 949.8 and 941px); only the box's last 12px and 3px are cut.
- In Mordekaiser vs Ornn and Ornn vs Mordekaiser, Ornn's level-14 note is cut mid-sentence.
- Riven vs Ornn's 8px at 1440x900 is only the page's bottom padding: its content ends 20px above the foot.
- The spec comment "Ornn vs Gwen is the tallest" holds if read narrowly: it is the tallest of the reversed curated pairs at 1440x900. At 1920x950, Renekton vs Ambessa is taller.
- Severity is debatable. The scroll is 34–104px, the five enemy tiles and Danger/Opportunity stay fully on screen, and Riot's notice is still visible in the sidebar.

title: For the import: a fact from Riot's text shows only its kind word. Its condition or form, and any disagreement between Riot's two texts, appear only in a hover tip
detail:
How it works now:
- RiotTextFact and RiotTextChip carry only {kind, clause, source}.
- import-riot-text.mjs keeps nothing else.
- FactChipView renders only the kind's word ('Stun'); the clause is in the InfoTip.
- abilityChips merges every clause of a kind into one chip.

The shape, from the unreviewed drafts used for the height measurement ((coordinator scratch)/mi-build/provisional/champions/Gnar.json):
- Gnar R 'stun' rests on 'Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned'.
- Gnar W 'stun' rests on 'Mega Gnar … stunning enemies'.

Both would read as a plain 'Stun' on the tile and on the Danger side, with no 'if it hits a wall' or 'Mega Gnar only'. The docs say Riot's description and tooltip disagree on at least six abilities. Such an ability would show two plain chips (for example Knock-up and Knock-back) with nothing saying Riot's texts differ. Glancing from a second monitor while playing, nobody hovers, so conditional facts read as unconditional.
fix:
- Carry a short qualifier through review, import and view, and show it on the chip ('Stun · hits a wall', 'Stun · Mega form').
- Mark a kind whose clauses come from texts that disagree ('Riot's texts differ').
- Keep the tip for the quoted clause.

verdict.reason:
The gap is real, and the finished review data makes it worse than the finding says. I reproduced it through the branch's own code, in memory, without editing anything.

The code (9cce9a33) carries only slot, kind, clause and source at every step:
- RiotTextFact, and RiotTextChip's {clause, source} list.
- importChampion pushes only those four fields.
- parseRiotText (src/server/matchup-intel/riot-text.ts) rebuilds only those four.
- chipWord returns RIOT_TEXT_KIND_WORDS[kind].
- The Details window lists the kind's word and its clauses.
Nothing in the branch's Matchup Intel code mentions qualifier, conditional, alsoDescribedAs or disagreements.

The finished review table (scratchpad mi/reviewed; DONE written 04:39 UTC, after the head at 03:03) has these markers:
- 68 qualifiers (4 with qualifierSource), 44 conditional, 11 alsoDescribedAs, and 7 slots where Riot's two texts disagree.
- 108 of 1,112 facts have a qualifier or the conditional marker; 82 of 173 champions are affected.
Its _summary.md says how the app must show each:
- the qualifier "with the fact, in Riot's words";
- the fixed marker "Conditional: see Riot's text";
- "also described as <kind>", with no second chip;
- for a disagreement, say Riot's two texts differ, show both quotes, never pick one.

What I ran:
- The branch's import refuses all 173 files as they are: `review` is a string, and the counts sit in reviewRecord.automatedReviewers. So the import step has to change the script anyway.
- With the record reshaped, all 1,112 facts import and none keeps a marker.
- Gnar W: the chip reads "Stun" and its tip is only "stunning enemies in an area." The qualifier "Mega Gnar" is gone even from the tip.
- Gnar R: "Stun" loses "Mega Gnar"; "hits a wall" survives only in the tip.
- Sion passive: "Heal" loses "After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate".
- Shaco R: the tip for "Fear" is "and Fear for […] second." with no Conditional marker.
- Camille E, Sion R and Zac R show no chip for the knock-up, stun or knock-back the texts dispute, and nothing says Riot's texts differ.

Today /resources/matchups?champion=Gnar&vs=Sion says "No reviewed facts for Gnar yet…". So the owner meets this as soon as the facts are imported, which is the next step. The owner's stated use is a second monitor while playing (decisions of 18 Nov).

Corrections to the finding:
1. Not "only a hover tip": the tip also opens on tap or focus, and the clauses are in the Details window. With the reviewed data, the qualifier is dropped altogether rather than tucked into the tip.
2. A disputed slot holds no fact of either kind, so it would not show "two plain chips". It shows neither, without saying why. The "Riot's texts differ" mark belongs on the slot, with both quotes.
3. The suggested labels 'hits a wall' and 'Mega form' break the review's rule of Riot's words only, never a condition of our own. It should read "Stun · Mega Gnar", the fixed "Conditional: see Riot's text", and "also described as Leap". The markers need carrying through importChampion, the types, parseRiotText, riotTextView, abilityChips, the chip, its tip, the Details window and the assembled sides.
4. The point about abilityChips merging clauses does not matter for the reviewed table, which has one fact per slot and kind.

Aside: on port 3871, /matchup-intel returns 404. This build serves the page at /resources/matchups (MATCHUP_INTEL_PATH).

Files are in (coordinator scratch)/mi-review2-refute-riot-text-qualifier/:
- import-check.mjs and import-check.out
- render-check.mts, render-check.out and render-check-2.out

title: At 200% text on phones a cooldown number breaks in the middle ('11' becomes '1' / '1 s')
detail:
Gwen vs Nidalee at 393×852, with the browser font size at 200% (32px):
- the Opportunity side's Gwen E line reads '13/12.5/12/11.5/1' and then '1 s' on the next line;
- Gwen Q's '6.5/5.75/5/4.25/3.5 s' breaks inside '3.5' at 320, 375 and 393px at 200%.

A reader can take the last rank as 1 s.

Cause: tightCooldownWords removes the spaces ('a/b/c'), and the page container sets [overflow-wrap:anywhere], so the browser breaks inside numbers.

Related, at 100% on a 320×568 phone: the tile lines wrap mid-sequence ('9 / 7.75 / 6.5 / 5.25 /' then '4 s'; '26 / 23.5 / 21 / 18.5 /' then '16 s'). They fit on one line at 375 and 393px.

Evidence (in (coordinator scratch)/mi-review2-owner/):
- pscroll/Gwen-vs-Nidalee__393x852__200__03.png
- phone/results-browser.json
fix: Allow breaks only after the slashes (a <wbr> or zero-width space after each '/'), and keep each number unbreakable (white-space: nowrap per value).

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The defect reproduces on the reviewed head (9cce9a33; the server on 3871 runs the 2dd104b7 build of 02:18 UTC and serves "13/12.5/12/11.5/11 s"). I measured each character's position on screen and checked the screenshots.

What I reproduced (Gwen vs Nidalee):
- Chromium with the browser font size at 32px:
  - 320×568 and 375×667: Q reads "6.5/5.75/5/4.25/3", then ".5 s" on the next line.
  - 390×844 and 393×852: Q reads "6.5/5.75/5/4.25/3.", then "5 s"; E reads "13/12.5/12/11.5/1", then "1 s".
- The same breaks appear with the root font-size emulation at 200%.
- WebKit at root 200% breaks the same way.

It reaches further than reported. A sweep of 12 pairs at 7 phone sizes, at 175% and 200%, also found these, on both the Danger and the Opportunity side:
- Ornn E "14/13.5/13/12.5/1", then "2 s";
- Ornn W "12/11.5/11/10.5/1", then "0 s";
- Renekton E "16/14.5/13/11.5/1", then "0 s".

These happen at 390 and 393px; Gwen Q breaks at 320 to 393px. None at 150% or 175%, and none at 360, 412 or 430px.

The cause is confirmed:
- The assembled-cooldown span has overflow-wrap: anywhere, inherited from the page container (page.tsx:46). It sits in a 239px box with 24px text, at the "8rem beside the key" layout.
- The tight string has no break point: no spaces, and a "/" stays with the digit after it.
- With overflow-wrap: normal on the span (changed only in my own browser), it no longer breaks inside a number but runs 20 to 39px past its box.
- With a <wbr> after each "/" plus normal, it wraps after a slash ("13/12.5/12/11.5/" then "11 s") and stays inside the box. So the suggested fix works.

Why the other refutation grounds fail:
- **Caused by this branch:** assembled.tsx and formatCooldownsTight do not exist on origin/main (5e37015b). Only the inherited overflow-wrap is older.
- **The owner would meet it:** docs/MATCHUP_INTEL.md "On a phone" and docs/RESPONSIVE.md claim that at 200% on 320 and 390px phones nothing is broken. Their audit only flags words of four or more letters, so it misses digits.
- **Not a misreading:** the page shows exactly the lines the finding quotes.
- **It will spread:** the coming import adds more lines with tight cooldowns.

One caveat: the "related" 100% wraps at 320px are ordinary breaks at the spaces between values, not inside a number. They are not a defect on their own, but the main claim stands. Severity minor is fair.

Evidence in (coordinator scratch)/mi-review2-acceptance/:
- run1/Gwen-vs-Nidalee__393x852__200__browser__1.png
- run1/Gwen-vs-Nidalee__320x568__200__browser__0.png
- run4-webkit/Darius-vs-Ornn__393x852__200__root__0.png
- run3.log
- the results-*.json files; the scripts are breaks.cjs and cause.cjs.

title: The assembled reference says "No curated briefing ... yet" when the pair has a curated briefing that is only hidden, and links to the pair the reader is already on
detail:
Affects: any curated pair whose briefing is hidden whole, either because its check is three patches old or because Riot changed every ability it rests on. In both cases the page draws the hidden-briefing panel and then the assembled reference under it.

How I reproduced it: rendered the page body on the server from the real curated files and the 16.22.1 copy of the ability data, with MatchupStatus and MatchupContent (tools/fresh.mts in my folder).

Case 1, Ambessa vs Renekton, game on 16.25.1 (three patches after the check):
- The panel reads: "This briefing is hidden: it was checked on patch 26.22, three patches ago, and not since."
- Right under it: "Assembled reference · Curated for Ambessa: [Ambessa vs Renekton] · No curated briefing for Ambessa vs Renekton yet."

Case 2, Gwen vs Ornn on 16.23.1 with every ability changed: same contradiction.

The curated link points at the page already shown. CuratedLinks is given no `current`, so the link is not marked as the current page, and a click only moves focus to the enemy slot, because go() returns early for the same pair.

On every other channel the page is right: its description says "its curated briefing is hidden, so each champion's own facts follow" and the announcement does too. So the only wrong claim is the visible one.

Not tested: matchup-content.test.ts:377 ("three patches since the check") does not check the assembled header.
fix: When view.matchup exists but nothing of it shows, give the assembled header a sentence of its own (for example "The curated briefing for X vs Y is hidden: ...") instead of "No curated briefing ... yet". Leave the current pair out of CuratedLinks, or mark it as the current page. Add an assertion to the expired and all-hidden tests.

verdict.reason:
Not refuted. I reproduced it on my own, and every part of the claim holds.

How I checked: tools/repro.mts renders the page body on the server, the way the page builds it, from the real curated files and the committed 16.22.1 ability copy (the reviewed-fact loader is in, and it is empty). tools/shot.cjs then draws that output in Chromium with the build's own CSS from :3871.
- Case 1, expired. Ambessa vs Renekton on 16.25.1 gives `recheck {patches:3, expired:true}`, `briefing:null`, `briefingShows:false`. Riven vs Mordekaiser on 16.25.1 and Ambessa vs Renekton on 17.1.1 give the same. The panel says "This briefing is hidden: it was checked on patch 26.22, three patches ago, and not since. It shows again once a person checks it." Directly under it, visible on desktop and phone: "Assembled reference · Curated for Ambessa: [Ambessa vs Renekton] · No curated briefing for Ambessa vs Renekton yet. Put together from each champion's own facts. No person has checked Ambessa vs Renekton as a pair."
- Case 2, every part hidden. Gwen vs Ornn on 16.23.1 with the cooldowns of Ornn E, Gwen W and Gwen Q changed gives "This briefing is hidden: Riot changed Ornn E, Gwen W and Gwen Q after it was checked." and then the same header.
- Controls behave correctly. At 16.22.1 and at two patches since the check, the curated pair shows its briefing with no assembled reference; Garen vs Darius shows the assembled reference.
- The header's only link goes to the pair already on screen (`?champion=Ambessa&vs=Renekton`), with no aria-current. Neither CuratedLinks call site passes `current`. On a plain click, PairLink calls preventDefault; goTo moves focus to the enemy slot; go() returns because `next` equals `shown`. I confirmed this from the code, not in a browser: the live server is on 26.22, so the hidden state cannot be reached there without changing its database.
- The sr-only description in page.tsx and announcementWords both say the briefing is hidden. MatchupStatus says only "Assembled reference".

Caused by this branch: yes. On origin/main, MatchupContent rendered `matchup ? <Briefing/> : <NoBriefing/>`. A hidden briefing therefore showed only its own panel, and the "No curated briefing … yet" line and its curated links appeared only when no matchup file existed. assembled.tsx is new, and the branch draws it under a hidden briefing with a fixed header. 2dd104b7 to 9cce9a33 changes docs only.

The owner will meet it:
- All three curated briefings were checked on 26.22. MAX_PATCHES_UNCHECKED = 2 stays by the owner's decision 9, so every one hides whole on the third patch after 26.22 unless a person re-checks it.
- The state is designed and tested (matchup-content.test.ts:377 and :298), and neither test asserts the assembled header. The docs give only the uncurated example header.
- The owner's decision 1 puts the "no person checked the pair" label on pairs without a matchup file. Decision 16 says coverage is "said as it is", and STANDARDS' honest-data rule applies.

Not a misreading. The claim is literal, and the same header contradicts itself: "Curated for Ambessa: Ambessa vs Renekton" stands beside "No curated briefing for Ambessa vs Renekton yet". The report understates one point: "No person has checked Ambessa vs Renekton as a pair" is also false in this state, so it is not the only wrong visible claim.

Severity: a real honest-data defect, but it is wrong words in a state reached later (about January 2027 at a two-week cadence, sooner if Riot changes the abilities involved), with nothing broken. "Moderate to major" seems fairer than a clear "major".

Note for the orchestrator: on this build /matchup-intel returns 404. The page is /resources/matchups (MATCHUP_INTEL_PATH), and it returns 200.

Files are in (coordinator scratch)/mi-review2-refute-hidden-briefing/:
- tools/repro.mts and tools/shot.cjs (the scripts)
- repro.log (the render output)
- case1-expired.html, case2-allhidden.html and control-*.html (the rendered bodies)
- shot-case1-expired-desktop.png, shot-case1-expired-phone.png and shot-case2-allhidden-desktop.png

title: The assembled reference shows checked facts of abilities Riot changed after the check, with no flag
detail:
kit.ts:119 computes `KitItem.flagged` (Riot changed this ability since the check), but KitLine never renders it. Elsewhere the page handles the same facts carefully:
- the curated briefing hides any point that rests on a changed ability;
- the tile shows "Changed since the check";
- the interactions fold and the level notes flag them.

Case 1, Riven vs Darius on 16.23.1 with Riot's cooldown for Riven's Valor (E) changed (tools/fresh2.mts):
- The Opportunity side lists "E · Mobility: Dash · 9/8/7/6/5 s" and "E · Defence: Shield".
- Their tips still read "Checked notes · Source: ...". Nothing on the side flags them.
- The only warning is in the folded "Your champion" summary ("Riot changed one ability after the check: its notes are flagged"). It does not name the ability, and Riven's tiles are folded away by default.

Case 2, Gwen vs Ornn on 16.23.1 with all abilities changed:
- The briefing says "This briefing is hidden: Riot changed Ornn W, Ornn passive, Ornn E ...".
- The Danger side directly under it shows Ornn's checked facts for those same abilities (for example "Slow: The fissure slows enemies it hits by 40% for 2 s."), unflagged.

When it happens: any patch that changes an ability of the six champions with checked notes, who include the owner's priority champions Ambessa, Gwen and Riven. That affects their 169 or so non-curated pairs each.
fix: Render item.flagged on KitLine (the same "Changed since the check" badge as the tile and the interactions fold), or treat flagged items the way the briefing does. Add a test: an assembled pair with one changed ability on each side.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The finding reproduces, it comes from this branch, the owner will meet it, and it is not a misreading.

**Code.** `kit.ts:119` sets `flagged = a.freshness === "changed-since"` on every KitItem, the group items included. The type's own comment says "they are flagged". But `KitLine` in `assembled.tsx` never reads `item.flagged`. The chip tip in `fact-chip.tsx` has no freshness line either, only "Checked notes · Source: …".
- The same KitItems are flagged elsewhere on the page. The interactions fold (`matchup-notes.tsx:36,47-50,66-68`) renders a flag from `kitOf().interactions`. The tile shows "Changed since the check". The level notes are flagged, and the briefing hides points that rest on a changed ability.
- On the assembled side, Riot-text (L3) facts whose text changed are hidden and the side says so. Checked (L2) facts of a changed ability get nothing.
- No unit or browser test covers the assembled reference with a changed ability. The docs do not say the omission is intended. MATCHUP_INTEL.md, "When a patch changes them", says that when Riot changes an ability "the notes are flagged as possibly out of date".

**Reproduction.** I rendered the page body the same way the page does: `buildMatchupPageView` and `MatchupContent`, with the committed notes. Riot's data was the offline Data Dragon copy moved to 16.23.1. The page itself feeds `buildMatchupPageView` its stored abilities, so injecting a changed copy is the same as the database holding a later version. I then showed those bodies in the live server's styles to take screenshots.
- **Riven vs Darius, Riven E's cooldown 1 s lower:** the Opportunity side lists "E Dash 9/8/7/6/5 s" and "E Shield" with no flag. The tips read "Checked notes · Source: …", and the Shield tip holds checked numbers ("70 to 170 (+110% bonus AD) by rank, for 1.5 seconds"). The tile is flagged but sits inside "Your champion", which is a `details` element with no `open`.
- **Gwen vs Ornn, every cooldown changed:** the page says "This briefing is hidden: Riot changed Ornn W, Ornn E, Ornn R, Gwen W, Ornn Q and Gwen Q after it was checked." Directly below, the Danger and Opportunity sides list those abilities' checked facts unflagged, including "Slow: The fissure slows enemies it hits by 40% for 2 s." On the same screen, Ornn's tiles all say "Changed since the check".
- **Darius vs Riven:** the Danger side is likewise unflagged. Here the enemy's flagged tile is visible beside it on a desktop.
- **A rework (Riven E given a new id and name):** the Opportunity side states Valor's old facts under the new ability's name, still with no flag.

**Will the owner meet it.** Yes. The hourly version-check job stores each new Data Dragon version on its own. Any change to the cooldown array, spell id, name, ranks or charges of the six champions with checked notes (Ambessa, Gwen, Riven, Renekton, Ornn, Mordekaiser) then shows like this. It lasts until a person re-checks the notes, which is a manual pull request. The notes keep showing even after the check expires. The case is weeks away, not hypothetical.

**Corrections to the finding (they do not change the verdict):**
- "The only warning is in the 'Your champion' summary" is not quite right. When the changed ability also has interaction or exception facts, as Riven E does, the Interactions fold's summary also says "1 changed since the check". It does not name the ability, and it is not on the Opportunity side.
- On this branch the page is at /resources/matchups. /matchup-intel returns 404 on the server at 3871.

**Severity.** Real, but it is an honest-data inconsistency rather than a breakage. After a cooldown-only change the chip words usually stay true; the risk is the checked numbers in the tips, and reworks. The fix is small, as the finding says.

**For the import.** Riot-text facts are already hidden and announced on the assembled side when their text changes, so the import needs nothing more here. The gap is only for checked facts.

title: The Production check's Matchup Intel facts will start failing every day once the game moves one patch past the check, with no code change
detail:
What the check asserts: matchupIntelFacts loads Riven vs Mordekaiser at 1440×900 (VIEWPORTS.desktop) and asserts `scrollHeight <= innerHeight`. Today the page has 43px to spare at that size.

How I measured: rendered the page body and the bar for later states on the server from the real data, put them into the live page at 3871, and measured (tools/states.mts, tools/inject.mjs). The current state measures exactly like the real page (900px, 43px to spare).

Results:

| State | 1440×900 | 1920×950 | 1920×1080 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Game on 26.23, nothing changed | 909px tall, 9px over | fits | fits |
| 26.23 with Mordekaiser Q's cooldown changed | 176px over | 11px over | fits |
| Three patches after the check (briefing expired) | 74px over | 88px over | fits |

In the first state the "Not re-checked for 26.23" badge pushes the bar's status onto a third line. Screenshot: shots/state-one-patch-1440x900.png.

A second fact can fail as well. If Riot changes enough abilities to hide every part of the briefing, the layer becomes "assembled" without `briefing-expired`, so "the curated briefing shows its threat and opportunity" fails.

title: Touch targets overlap: on phones and tablets part of a visible chip or ability key belongs to its neighbour (axe WCAG 2.2 target-size: serious)
detail:
Cause: chips (Badge with `touch-target`) and key links (AbilityRefLink) are 24px tall. On a coarse pointer their ::after hit area is 44px. Rows sit 2–4px apart (gap-1, space-y-0.5), so the next row's hit area, which is drawn later and so sits on top, covers the bottom of the row above.

Measured with elementFromPoint on Chromium, 375×667 touch (tools/touch.mjs, tools/scan.mjs):
- Riven vs Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser's passive chips:
  - "% max health aura" (139×24): 28px of tap height of its own; 7px of its visible box opens "Three stacks to activate".
  - "Three stacks to activate": 29px of its own.
  - "Stack display hidden ...": 31px of its own.
- Riven vs Darius, Opportunity side:
  - the "Passive" key (62×24): 22px of its own; 13px of its visible box opens the R line's "Bonus AD for 15 s" tip instead of jumping to the passive tile.
  - the "Q" key: 9px of it go to "W".

Scope: 15 mis-hit controls on Riven vs Mordekaiser and 7 on Riven vs Darius at 390×844; 6 and 7 on a 768 touch tablet. Same on Ornn vs Gwen, Riven vs Renekton and Ambessa vs Aatrox. The two "interactions and exceptions" summaries overlap in the same way.

axe with the wcag22aa tag reports target-size (serious) on the default phone view of Riven vs Mordekaiser. With every fold open it also does on Ornn vs Gwen, Riven vs Darius and Riven vs Riven. STANDARDS asks for WCAG 2.2 AA and 44px on touch screens.

Why CI misses it: quality.spec.ts and live-check.mjs run axe with only the WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 tags, and quality.spec's accessibility tests run on the desktop project only.
fix: On pointer-coarse, give wrapped chip rows and assembled lines enough row gap (about 20px) that 44px areas do not overlap, or cap the ::after so it never reaches a neighbour. Add `wcag22aa` (target-size) to a phone-size axe pass of Matchup Intel.

title: The importer pins Data Dragon's untrimmed ability name while the app trims it: Bel'Veth breaks the import
detail:
Cause: riotTexts() takes `entry.passive.name` raw. The app stores names through `z.string().trim()` (abilities.ts:146), and so does the offline copy.

In Data Dragon 16.22.1, Bel'Veth's passive is "Death in Lavender " with a trailing space. It is the only such name.

How I found it: I converted all 1,092 rows of the review's accepted batches (mi/reviewed) into a table and ran the importer with `--out` into my folder. It wrote Belveth.json with P = {"name":"Death in Lavender "}, while the copy has "Death in Lavender".

- riot-text.test.ts's pin check (`toEqual({ name: a.name, textHash })`) fails, which blocks the all-or-nothing import.
- If the review recorded the trimmed name, importChampion refuses the whole table (I reproduced this with a trailing space on Darius P).
- If that slot ever gets facts, riotTextView hides them as "renamed" and the page says "Riot renamed Passive after the review", which is false.
fix: Trim (and collapse whitespace in) names in riotTexts() and in the abilityText comparison, exactly as compactChampionAbilities does.
